ABOUT ROCKET LAB

Rocket Lab is the end-to-end space company building rockets, spacecraft, and critical subsystems that keep the world connected, protected, expand humanity’s reach to the Moon, Mars, and beyond. We move fast, build real hardware for meaningful missions, and make the impossible routine. Come shape the future with us.

CONTRACTOR PROGRAM SECURITY OFFICER (CPSO)

Based onsite at Rocket Lab's headquarters in Long Beach, CA, the Contractor Program Security Officer (CPSO) is responsible for developing, implementing, supervising, and maintaining program security for selected Department of War (DoW) and Intelligence Community (IC) programs. You will serve as the primary contractor security point of contact for your assigned programs, partnering with the Government Program Security Officer (GPSO), the Corporate FSO/CPSO, and the site security team to keep program operations compliant. You will produce deliverables for internal leadership, the board of directors, customers, and investors. You will support programmatic activities for classified launch campaigns and classified payload and space vehicle development. You will address program security requirements across all security disciplines, including physical, information, personnel, operations security (OPSEC), and launch integration security.

Who we are

Samsara (NYSE: IOT) is the pioneer of the Connected Operations™ Cloud, which is a platform that enables organizations that depend on physical operations to harness Internet of Things (IoT) data to develop actionable insights and improve their operations. At Samsara, we are helping improve the safety, efficiency and sustainability of the physical operations that power our global economy. Representing more than 40% of global GDP, these industries are the infrastructure of our planet, including agriculture, construction, field services, transportation, and manufacturing — and we are excited to help digitally transform their operations at scale.

Working at Samsara means you’ll help define the future of physical operations and be on a team that’s shaping an exciting array of product solutions, including Video-Based Safety, Vehicle Telematics, Apps and Driver Workflows, and Equipment Monitoring. As part of a recently public company, you’ll have the autonomy and support to make an impact as we build for the long term.

About the role:

This is a high energy role in which you will bring the Internet of Things to small to medium size customers, building Samsara's business and bringing the benefits of sensor data to customers. Typical sales will be $5k to $20k, and typically involve proof of concepts, multiple stakeholders, multi-faceted pricing negotiations, and selling to owners, safety and operational managers.

This is a remote position open to candidates residing in the US.

You should apply if: 

• You want to impact the industries that run our world: Your efforts will result in real-world impact—helping to keep the lights on, get food into grocery stores, and most importantly, ensure workers return home safely.

• Your mantra is #alwaysbeprospecting: The world

Natera is building apps and services that run inside the clinician's EHR. This is a hands-on role.
You will build SMART on FHIR apps that launch from Epic, Oracle Health (Cerner) and other
EHRs, the FHIR services and data model behind them, and CDS Hooks services that bring
Natera ordering and results into the provider's workflow. You will work in a small team with
product and our wider EHR integration group, and you will handle patient data under HIPAA
every day.

• Build and ship SMART on FHIR apps: EHR launch and standalone launch, OAuth 2.0 with
PKCE, backend services authorization, scopes and token handling.
• Design and build the server side: FHIR R4 APIs, mapping to our internal data model,
profiles and extensions.

• Take apps through EHR vendor onboarding and go-live, starting with Epic (Vendor
Services and Showroom), then Oracle Health and others. Work with health system IT on
build and testing.
• Handle PHI correctly in storage, caching, logging and tracing: minimum necessary data,
encryption, audit trails, no PHI in logs.

Normal Computing is building a new paradigm of AI hardware to power human progress. We build inference servers and rack-scale systems designed to increase efficiency and interactivity. We use AI to accelerate silicon co-design and product development.

Our primary offices are in New York City, London, and Mountain View.




THE ROLE

Normal's hardware runs the most memory-bound parts of large-model inference inside memory itself, rather than shuttling weights to a processor. The software that makes this programmable doesn't exist yet in any standard form. The runtime is the layer the rest of that software runs through: it is how compiled programs get loaded, scheduled, and executed on our hardware. You will own its design and much of its implementation, and set its technical direction.



This is a senior, hands-on role. Our chip is pre-silicon, so you will build the runtime against our simulators and FPGA prototypes first, behind one interface, so that software above the runtime doesn't change when silicon arrives.




WHAT YOU WILL OWN

 - Runtime Architecture: Own the design of the runtime: device management, memory allocation and host-device transfer, executable loading, and command submission. Success means the compiler and serving layers program our hardware through one stable interface.

 - Hardware Abstraction: Hide the differences between simulators, FPGA prototypes, silicon, and later hardware generations behind that interface.

 - Device State: Manage the state that lives on our hardware between requests, such as resident model weights, so the serving layer can rely on it.

 - Performance: Keep runtime overhead off the critical path for LLM inference, measured by end-to-end latency and throughput.
